name: Gas-fired and gas-conversion circulating fluidized bed boiler
description: Circulating fluidized bed boiler in which fine solids are suspended in a high-velocity gas stream and circulated through a cyclone or U-beam collector back to the furnace. Commercial CFB lines from the OEMs read are dominated by solid and multi-fuel designs; natural-gas firing is evidenced as a solid-fuel-to-gas conversion offering and as gas firing in a circulating-bed alumina calciner, not as a dedicated gas-fired boiler product. Primary source: https://www.babcock.com/home/products-services/steam-generators/circulating-fluidized-bed-boilers

Thermal power page: efficient mixing and relatively low combustion temperatures contribute to low emissions

'With CFB technology, the flue gas velocity in the furnace is higher and the bed is expanded and entrained with the flow. The bed material flows with the flue gas through the furnace, after which the material is separated by cyclones and returned to the lower furnace.'
'The efficient mixing and relatively low combustion temperatures contribute to low emissions of carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, and nitric oxides.'

'CFB technology also allows an extremely wide range of fuels to be fired in the same unit.'; BFB EcoFluid: 'a variety of clean biomass fuels (bark, agricultural, forestry, and sawmill residuals) ... demolition wood, refuse-derived fuels, peat, various sludges, etc.'
